paper.title: DiffQRCoder: Diffusion-based Aesthetic QR Code Generation with Scanning Robustness Guided Iterative Refinement

official_public_code_observations.public_perceptual_loss_autograd_issue: torch.tensor(list_of_losses) detaches the listed scalar losses in ordinary PyTorch autograd; Prooftag uses torch.stack to preserve the intended gradient

e044_setup.loss_profile: official upstream ScanningRobustLoss + scanaware_v2 perturbation ensemble + full-module margin
e044_setup.authoritative_scanner: qr-verify@0.2.0, 37 presets, conservative repeated exact-payload scoring

ambiguities_or_reproducibility_gaps.detail: The paper says 100 GPT-4 prompts were used, but the exact corpus, seeds and per-prompt selection policy are not provided in the paper.
The paper specifies QArt(Stage1,target) but does not provide enough information to reconstruct the authors' exact target generation choices from the PDF alone.
Algorithm 1 specifies VAE encode plus Gaussian noise at T, but exact random seeds/noise realizations for the reported 100 samples are not published.
The paper reports 80-pixel padding while the official public runner defaults to 78 pixels.
The public runner uses 2, the public pipeline signature exposes 10, while Table 7 reports 3 for the 99% configuration.
The paper reports gamma=1000 and lambda=0.01 but does not clearly bind the number of SR-MPGD updates used for every reported table result.
The paper describes VAE decoding as the manifold projection. The released SR-MPGD path is direct SGD on the latent and has no explicit projection/trust-region operator.
Paper Eq.1 is centered at 0.5, whereas the released ScanningRobustLoss uses asymmetric 0.45/0.65 pixel thresholds.
The paper gives sigma=floor((s-1)/5), which is 3 for s=20; released code instantiates cv2.getGaussianKernel with sigma=1.5 and then clips low weights.

Algorithm 1 conditionally applies SRPG while QR module error exceeds the error-correction capacity tau. This conditional gate is not evident in the released Stage-2 loop, which computes the SRPG score every step.
The paper names qr-verify but does not pin the package version or fully specify preset ordering/aggregation. E044 pins the project adapter protocol and exact payload matching.

ambiguities_or_reproducibility_gaps.topic: Device SSR protocol differs from software SSR
ambiguities_or_reproducibility_gaps.detail: Appendix D.2 scans 30 QR images ten times on each scanner/device. This is not numerically identical to E044's 37-preset software robustness score.
The released PerceptualLoss wraps scalar MSE tensors using torch.tensor([...]), which ordinarily detaches them; the paper intended LPIPS gradient therefore cannot be assumed reproduced without a fix.
The paper names checkpoints but does not pin all model file hashes, diffusers/PyTorch versions and exact repository revisions needed for byte-level reproduction.
